svg.text: Institutional Decision Lifecycle
1. Define the decision
Specify the service problem, population, complete intervention, realistic
comparators, outcomes, value mechanism, stakeholders, and accountable
authority.
2. Assess readiness and data
Evaluate institutional capability, data fitness, provenance, interoperability,
lawful access, resilience, technical debt, workflow capacity, and prerequisite
investment.
3. Establish evidence and quality requirements
Define validation, reporting, appraisal, quality-control, accreditation,
patient-safety, and independent-assurance requirements before consequential
use.
4. Model cost, value, affordability, and HTA
Estimate lifecycle cost, pricing exposure, benefit realization, cost-
effectiveness, budget impact, affordability, distribution, reimbursement, and
HTA implications.
5. Select the decision model and characterize
uncertainty
Choose a decision or simulation structure that matches the causal and
operational problem; document assumptions, verification, sensitivity,
scenarios, thresholds, and value of information.
6. Assess governance and institutional risk
Evaluate accountability, human oversight, ethics, equity, privacy,
cybersecurity, resilience, trust, contestability, communication, and
institutional risk as connected requirements.
7. Procure and contract
Translate the defined service need into vendor evidence requirements, due
diligence, acceptance testing, pricing, audit rights, update control,
continuity, portability, remedies, and exit.
8. Implement, monitor, and control change
Use staged implementation, role and competency design, post-deployment
monitoring, algorithmovigilance, incident reconstruction, corrective action,
material-change review, and renewal controls.
9. Apply circular and sustainable-value analysis
Assess resource stewardship, circular procurement, asset life, environmental
and material effects, residual value, resilience, equity, rebound, recovery,
and responsible disposition.
10. Assemble the decision record and renew or
retire
Integrate evidence, economics, governance, implementation, monitoring,
circularity, conditions, dissent, and accountability into a versioned decision
record and make an explicit continue, redesign, restrict, replace, or retire
renewed decision and organizational learning
